chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us from his father from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi from Aban and other than him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said:

Indeed, I pray for mercy for three -- and it is their right to be prayed for mercy: a person dear to his community who is afflicted with humiliation after glory, a rich person who is afflicted with need after needlessness, and a scholar who is undervalued by his people and the ignorant.

key_terms.عزيز قوم: A person dear and honored by their community -- one who held social prestige
key_terms.مذلة: Humiliation, abasement -- the loss of dignity and social standing
key_terms.يستخف: To undervalue, belittle, treat lightly -- a form of disrespect toward knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about three types of people who deserve mercy and compassion?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) expresses compassion for three categories of people whose circumstances have dramatically declined: someone once honored in their community who falls into humiliation, a wealthy person who becomes impoverished, and a scholar who is belittled by his own people and the ignorant. The Imam emphasizes that such people rightly deserve compassion due to the painful contrast between their former and current states.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Ziyad al-Azdi from Aban and other than him from Abu `Abdillah (as). He said:

I pray for mercy for three – and it is their right to be prayed for mercy: (1) a person dear to his community who is afflicted with humiliation after glory, (2) a rich person that is afflicted with a need after needlessness, and (3) a scholar that is undervalued by his people and the ignorant.
